statement: The kept element conversion surface is narrower than the one it replaces, and the difference only became visible because the case was compiled against it instead of being deleted with the library.

keptSurface.declaration: public static T? GetObject<T>(this JsonElement jsonElement, JsonSerializerOptions options) where T : class
keptSurface.companion: Transform<T>(this object, JsonSerializerOptions) at the same file, line 26

removedSurface.constraint: none; a value type was accepted

measured.compilerFinding: error CS0452: int must be a reference type to be used as T in GetObject<T>
measured.howItSurfaced: The old case converted a bare scalar. Re-pointing it at the kept surface did not compile, which is what a deletion would have hidden.

productConsumers.conclusion: Every product caller converts a message or a dictionary, never a scalar. The constraint therefore describes what the product needs and removes no capability the product uses.

disposition: No product change. The scalar case is not restated on the kept surface, because the product does not offer scalar conversion there; a caller needing a scalar reads it from the element directly. The surface now has its own test, which it did not have before.
